title: Hosted API — Amortized GPU & License Allocation (working sheet)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet tries to make the fixed-cost allocation explicit for Hosted API unit economics. Many optimize sheets focus on per-token marginal costs (GPU-seconds per token) but we lack a consistent method to spread GPU-hour reservations, enterprise license fees, and support/monitoring amortization across customers, models, and regions.

High-level approach (proposal):
1) Separate costs into two buckets: Fixed amortized (reserved GPU hours, licensing, monitoring/infra overhead) and Variable (per-token inference compute, egress, storage).
2) Define allocation keys for fixed costs: a) committed GPU-hours by pool, b) customer segment weight (usage + SLA tier), c) model footprint (tokens/sec equivalence).
3) Compute an "amortized add-on" per-request and convert to ppk / per-token uplift. Add to variable cost to get end-to-end COGS.

Assumptions & constants (editable):
- Reserved dedicated GPU hours (hosted pools): 45,600 GPU-hours / month (mixed A10G & T4 equivalent).
- Enterprise license + infra retention fee (monitoring, 3rd-party licenses): $120k / month.
- Average effective GPU $/hour (amortized across HW mix + infra): $3.80 / GPU-hour.
- Variable compute avg: 0.000012 GPU-hours per token (approx 0.043 sec per 512 tokens on avg model).
- Avg tokens per request: 850 (weighted across chat/generation/embeddings truncated).
- Network egress + misc per-request avg: $0.0025.
- Billing month base: 30 days.

Allocation methodology (step-by-step):
A) Compute fixed pool monthly cost = reserved GPU-hours * $/GPU-hour + license fee + fixed infra ops overhead (assume $18k).
   - Example: 45,600 * $3.80 = $173,280 + 120,000 + 18,000 = $311,280 / month.
B) Define allocation base: choose either 'requests', 'tokens', or 'compute-equivalent' (tokens * per-token GPU usage).
   - Quick proxy: compute-equivalent gives better fairness across short vs long requests.
   - Compute-equivalent = total_tokens_month * 0.000012 (GPU-hours).
C) Amortized rate per GPU-hour = fixed pool monthly cost / reserved GPU-hours (sanity check).
   - Using example: 311,280 / 45,600 = $6.83 per reserved GPU-hour (note this includes license & infra).
D) Translate back to per-token amortized uplift: per-token_amort = per_gpu_hour_rate * per-token_gpu_hours (0.000012).
   - Example: 6.83 * 0.000012 = $0.00008196 per token => ~0.08196 ppk (per 1k tokens = $0.08196).

Worked example (by customer segment & model family):
- Input monthly totals (sample, editable):
  * Total tokens month (hosted): 3,200,000,000 tokens
  * Total reserved GPU-hours: 45,600 (as above)
  * Model mix: family A (high-throughput small models) 40% tokens; family B (large-context L2) 35%; family C (embeddings) 25%

Compute-equivalent total = 3.2B * 0.000012 = 38,400 GPU-hours consumed (note reserved > consumed — idle/burst capacity accounted separately).
Per-token amort from fixed pool (alternative compute-based allocation) = fixed_pool_cost / (total_tokens_month) = 311,280 / 3.2B = $0.000097275 per token => ~0.0973 ppk (slightly higher due to license inclusion).

Per-segment breakdown (illustrative):
- Family A (40% tokens = 1.28B tokens): amort = 1.28B * 0.000097275 = $124,512 => per-1k tokens uplift = $0.0973
- Family B (35% = 1.12B tokens): amort = $108,768
- Family C (25% = 800M tokens): amort = $77,820

Combine with variable marginal compute (example):
- Variable compute per token = 0.000012 GPU-hours * $3.80 = $0.0000456 => 0.0456 ppk
- Add network/misc per token (0.0025 / avg tokens 850 ~ $0.00000294 per token => 0.00294 ppk) — NOTE this is small and approximate
- Total COGS per token (simple sum): amortized_per_token (0.0973) + variable_compute (0.0456) + network (0.00294) =~ 0.1458 ppk.

Edge cases / capacity inefficiency add-ons: 
- Idle reserve weight: if reserved GPU-hours > consumed, allocate an "idle premium" to pools with heavy SLA requirements: idle_premium_rate = (reserved - consumed) * per_gpu_hour_rate / total_tokens => in example reserved(45,600) - consumed(38,400) = 7,200 idle hours -> 7,200 * 6.83 = $49,176 / 3.2B = +0.0154 ppk
- Burst buffer: if we want to split 20% of license into "burst bucket" rather than base amort, we can credit back to on-demand pricing.

Sensitivity scenarios (quick UX grid):
- S1: +15% token growth (tokens -> 3.68B) holding reserved constant => amortized per token drops to 0.0000846 (0.0846 ppk) ; total COGS ~0.132 ppk.
- S2: +20% license fee (license -> $144k) => fixed_pool_cost -> 335,280 => per-token amort rises to 0.000104775 (0.1048 ppk).
- S3: GPU price shock +25% ($/GPU-hour -> $4.75) => fixed_pool_cost 45,600*4.75 + 120k + 18k = 344,400 => per-token amort ~0.0001076 (0.1076 ppk).
- S4: Model mix shift toward long-context (Family B -> 55% tokens, Family A 25%) increases avg tokens per req and may increase variable compute share; recompute per-token GPU-hours accordingly.

Operational notes and heuristics we should bake into Console: 
- Present both allocation views: per-token amort (simple) and compute-equivalent amort (fairer for short vs long requests).
- Expose "idle premium" toggle for Dedicated/reserved customers.
- Allow customers to opt into paying direct reserved share (commitment discounts) vs pay uplift in per-token pricing.
- Tag models with "allocation class" (latency-critical, best-effort, embeddings) — used to determine which pools carry more fixed-cost weight.

Recommendations (near-term):
1) Run this sheet as a 30-day rolling job to compute amortized ppk and show historic trend in Console under Cost -> Amortization.
2) Add a flag in pricing UI to show "amortized uplift" separately from marginal unit price so customers see what portion is fixed allocation.
3) Experiment: price a "commitment product" where customers take on a share of reserved GPU-hours; compare unit price (ppk) to default uplift.
4) Short-term ops: investigate regional skew — APAC GPU $/hour is 12% higher; if >20% of tokens originate there we should consider region-specific amort tables.

Open questions / TODOs (team):
- [ ] Diego: run a sample 3-month token & GPU-hours extract from billing telemetry (JIRA INF-2119) to populate baseline numbers by region/model/segment.
- [ ] Priya: validate per-token GPU-hour proxy for large-context models (0.000012) with serving-runtime counters (PR 548 in repo).
- [ ] Product: decide default allocation base (tokens vs compute-equivalent) for public docs.
- [ ] Ops: confirm monthly reserved GPU-hours across pools and whether we should amortize license per-pool or global.

Notes / quick math sanity checks: 
- If customers prefer per-call visibility, we can present amortized $/call by converting tokens->avg tokens per call by model family. 
- Keep a conservative buffer: treat 10% of reserved capacity as "buffer" not billable and allocate its cost to enterprise license pool.

Last thoughts (working doc style):
- This is intentionally conservative and includes license + infra in the fixed pool; we can create a separate "platform fee" line in pricing if marketing prefers clearer separation.
- Need to iterate with Finance to make the per-month fixed figure (license + infra + ops) auditable.

-- end of working sheet --

(Quick edit history: Maya initial draft 2025-02-12; Diego numbers updated 2025-02-20; sensitivity scenarios added 2025-02-28; doc marked draft for feedback 2025-03-01)
